what_happened: In slow highway traffic, the ego was told to go LEFT but stayed partly in its lane, behind and slightly left of the slow grey van ahead (actor 13). Over the last 2 s the gap closed from 6.4 m to 3.9 m while the ego held about 2 m/s without braking further, and its front-right clipped the van's rear as it finally shifted left. The rear contact came only after that front collision.

The route command switched to RIGHT and the route bent right, but the policy kept its trajectory straight and slightly left while slowing from 23 to 16 m/s. By 6.7 s it was 4.9 m off the recorded path and had driven onto the nose of the raised median island between the lanes. The camera view was clean beforehand, so this is a policy path-following error, not a rendering problem.

With a LEFT command, the ego started a slow lane change to the left from behind car 21, into the lane where car 24 was stopped or creeping in traffic. It moved its nose into that lane without leaving room and hit car 24's rear corner with its front at about 2.7 m/s, while the gap had shrunk to about 4 m.

On a straight highway (command STRAIGHT, then RIGHT), the policy's plan swung left out of the recorded lane after handoff. The ego cut into the adjacent left lane and sideswiped actor 41, which was coming up alongside from behind-left (lateral collision at 6.5 s, about 2 m off the recorded path).

The command was RIGHT and the route (green) curved right toward the right-turn lanes, but the policy kept its plan (orange) straight ahead and slightly left. While slowing down behind lead vehicle 9 (which was in a lane to its right), it drifted left and left the drivable area at the nose of the left median just before the stop line, about 7.6 m from the recorded path.

On a highway that bends left, the ego braked from about 29.6 to 16 m/s but kept heading straight instead of following the curve. It crossed the right edge line onto the shoulder toward the guardrail and was off the road at 7.0 s, 3.8 m from the human path, even though the route said LEFT and its planned path followed the curve.

The ego was in the rightmost lane, braking gently from about 15 to 11 m/s, when the road began curving slightly left. Its planned path kept going straight and then wiggled to the right, so it drifted across the right lane edge onto the shoulder and was flagged offroad at 6.9s, about 0.7 m from the recorded human path.

On a multi-lane highway, with the route command STRAIGHT and then RIGHT, the policy planned a path veering left across lanes, away from the recorded path. The ego drifted about 5 m left into the adjacent lane and struck vehicle 28 with its front at 7.2 s.

The ego was in the left lane at about 28 m/s and slowing. It kept heading slightly left and crossed the yellow edge line onto the left shoulder, while the recorded human path and the RIGHT route command went to the right. There were no actors nearby and the camera view was clear, so the policy simply steered off the drivable area.

On a multi-lane highway with a STRAIGHT and then RIGHT command, the policy moved left out of its lane while the recorded path stayed straight and bore slightly right. At 6.5 s it cut into the adjacent left lane and sideswiped vehicle 41, which was alongside and slightly behind it.

After the 4.7 s handoff on a wet multi-lane highway, the ego left its lane and drifted left, while the recorded path stayed straight and then went right. It then side-swiped actor 41, which was traveling in the adjacent left lane just beside and behind it. The ego was going about 5.7 m/s and was 1.9 m off the human trajectory at the time of contact.

In slow, dense traffic with a LEFT command, the ego (about 3 m/s) tried to merge left from the right lane toward the route lane. Its planned path cut into the side of vehicle 24, which was close ahead in the left lane, and the ego's front struck it at 7.4 s.

The route command was LEFT in slow, queued traffic, and the ego's plan swung left toward the lane where car 24 sat stopped or creeping ahead. The ego kept moving at about 3 m/s as it cut across the lane line, and its front hit the rear of car 24 (the gap closed from 9 m to 4 m in the last second). The camera only breaks up at the moment of impact, and the rear contact came after the front collision.

The ego was in the rightmost lane, slowing from about 15 to 11 m/s with no lead vehicle close by. The road bends gently left, but the policy's planned path stayed straight and wobbled toward the right curb instead of following the recorded path, which curved left, so the ego went over the right lane edge at 6.9s, about 0.7 m off the recorded trajectory.

The ego was going straight in the rightmost lane at about 11–15 m/s and slowing as the road bent gently left. Its planned path (orange) kinked right toward the curb instead of following the lane, and the ego's right side crossed the road edge at 6.9 s. It was only about 0.7 m from the recorded human path, so this was a marginal edge violation, not a large departure.

In slow highway traffic with a LEFT command, the ego steered right toward the next lane, into the silver van (actor 13) moving alongside it. Its front clipped the van at about 1.9 m/s while about 2 m off the recorded path; the rear contact came later.

In slow, dense highway traffic, the ego was ordered to go LEFT and slowly pulled out from behind actor 13 toward the left lane, where the human drove. It stayed about 1.9 m right of the human's path and moved too little laterally, so its front-right corner clipped the rear-left of actor 13 at about 1.6 m/s.

The command was RIGHT, and the recorded human moved over into the right lane. The ego instead slowed from about 29 to 19 m/s and drifted slightly left until it crossed the yellow left edge line onto the shoulder at 7.2 s, with no other actors nearby. The camera view was a little blurry at the left edge but the road was clear, so the policy is to blame.

On a clear, straight road with no lead vehicle, the ego slowed from about 29 to 19 m/s. Meanwhile it drifted left onto and across the yellow center line, even though the command had changed to RIGHT and the recorded path angled right. It went offroad on the left side at 7.1 s, about 2 m from the human's path.
